_comment: State the recorded conversation must leave behind. Asserted as a subset:
every field here must be present with this value, and the database may know
more. Only fields the recorded tool results revealed, or state that follows
necessarily from them, are asserted.
_key_columns declares how each table is addressed, so a row is identified by
a stable business key rather than by position in the snapshot. case_note_log
is a view that gives a single-column key to a table whose primary key is a
pair.
The two refunds are asserted unchanged. Policy forbids raising a second
refund while a trace is open, so a correct handling of this call leaves the
money exactly where it was and records why.
This document is read by both layers and everything in it has to be an
outcome rather than a route. section_read_log is therefore not asserted
here, although the recording drives it to three reads on each of the two
sections: reads_served counts how many times the agent looked, which is the
one thing the grading layer must not score. The conformance layer already
pins the read cursor far harder than an assertion could, because each depth
returns a different payload and the replay is byte-exact, so a cursor that
advanced wrongly fails env_check.sh on the wire.
The confirmation's status is asserted, but as a set rather than as one
value. A notification's delivery state is collected by looking at it: a
get_order that includes 'notifications' runs _advance_notification and moves
the message on to the next receipt, so an agent that checks whether its own
email went out would fail a single-valued assertion for reading. The
refund_trace_confirmation template hands the message over as 'sent' and its
delivery progression ends at 'delivered', so those two are the whole of what
a correct run can leave behind and either of them is accepted. The set still
asserts something real: it says a message actually went out and that it did
not fail, which is what the caller was promised, while saying nothing about
how many times anybody looked at it.
status_index is not asserted. It is a bare read counter with no outcome
meaning, and it is one of the two columns the damage policy drops from the
row hash for exactly that reason.
